Looking at the test image, I can see:
- Soybean pods that are dark brown/tan, somewhat shriveled
- Stems that are uniformly dark brown/thin
- Overall plant has a late-season dried appearance with darkened pods
- No obvious white mold, no visible black sclerotia, no leaf symptoms visible

The Diaporthe reference shows a similar pattern of overall plant drying and stem/pod darkening, with the disease causing pod blight and stem discoloration at maturity.

Key reasoning:
- The uniformly dark brown pods across the plant is consistent with pod and stem blight (Diaporthe)
- Stems appear dark brown and dried, consistent with Diaporthe stem blight
- The shriveled/collapsed pod appearance matches Diaporthe which causes premature pod darkening
- No white mold growth (rules out White_Mold), no visible sclerotia (rules out Charcoal_Rot), no distinct spot lesions (rules out Anthracnose)
